title: arxiv_2507.10172v1
universal_lens: Latent space embedding via CNN-LSTM autoencoders unifies sequential play trace data with unsupervised feature extraction, enabling domain-free style classification. Unified tensorial representation of game states and actions via feature channels and spatial dimensions.
gsi_mapping: Bayesian inference on latent play embeddings enables probabilistic style classification, reducing expert bias through conformal predictive uncertainty quantification. Bayesian inference on game state tensors enables probabilistic action prediction through conformal predictive distributions.
gse_mapping: Situational reasoning maps play trace sequences to state transitions in latent space, supporting dynamic agent behavior synthesis and adaptive gameplay. Situational reasoning maps game states to transition kernels over action space using derived spatial and numerical features.

primitives.name: Play Style Autoencoder
primitives.verbatim_quote: In this study, we explore the use of unsupervised CNN-LSTM autoencoder models to obtain latent representations directly from low-level play trace data in MicroRTS.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'X': 'high-dimensional play trace trajectory (dimension d)', 'Z': 'latent representation (dimension k)', 'E': 'encoding function', 'D': 'decoding function'}
primitives.assumptions: Sequential temporal structure of play traces is preserved; low-level data contains sufficient style-discriminative information.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When input data lacks temporal coherence or domain-specific features.

layer2.mapping: Autoencoder latent space Z is isomorphic to play style manifold under unsupervised learning.
layer2.telemetry: Reconstruction error and cluster separability in Z

primitives.name: Latent Style Separation
primitives.verbatim_quote: We demonstrate that this approach yields a meaningful separation of different game playing agents in the latent space, reducing reliance on domain expertise and its associated biases.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'S_i': 'style class i', 'Z_i': 'latent representation subset for S_i', 'd(Z_i, Z_j)': 'distance between style clusters'}
primitives.assumptions: Different play styles induce distinct latent distributions; separation is measurable via distance metrics.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When latent space fails to distinguish between agent classes due to overfitting or poor encoding.

layer2.mapping: Kernel density estimation on Z induces style kernel functions K(S_i).
layer2.telemetry: Silhouette score and inter-cluster variance in Z

primitives.name: Style-Guided Exploration
primitives.verbatim_quote: This latent space is then used to guide the exploration of diverse play styles within studied AI players.

primitives.assumptions: Latent space supports continuous exploration; diversity is encoded in Z distribution.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When G does not maintain coverage of Z-manifold or leads to local optima.

layer2.mapping: Exploration policy G is isomorphic to style diversity generator in Z.
layer2.telemetry: Diversity entropy and coverage of Z by generated trajectories

primitives.name: Domain-Free Style Identification
primitives.verbatim_quote: This removes the need for handcrafted features and reduces reliance on domain expertise, allowing play styles to be identified directly from data.
primitives.assumptions: Data-driven feature learning is sufficient for style discrimination; no prior domain knowledge required.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When data is insufficiently rich or mislabeled for unsupervised learning.

primitives.name: Tensorial Game State Representation
primitives.verbatim_quote: Data Description Our data is represented like [14] with modifications: 1) We unify the direction parameters into a single direction parameter to reduce dimensionality without loss of information.

primitives.breakdown_regime: When feature channels exceed memory constraints or when spatial resolution becomes insufficient.

layer2.mapping: Maps game state to a tensor (h, w, co) where each cell encodes categorical and numerical features via one-hot and scalar encodings respectively.
layer2.telemetry: Accuracy of state reconstruction from tensor input.

primitives.name: CNN-LSTM Autoencoder
primitives.verbatim_quote: CONCLUSION This work explores the use of CNN-LSTM autoencoders to learn embeddings of low-level representations of play traces to identify play styles, reducing reliance on domain expertise during feature creation.
primitives.assumptions: Stationary ergodic data streams, Lipschitz continuous encoder/decoder functions, and a bottleneck layer enforcing information bottleneck.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Autoencoder capacity exceeds optimal compression rate leads to overfitting; capacity falls below critical threshold causes information loss.

layer2.mapping: The learned lower-dimensional latent code \(z_t\) directly parameterizes posterior predictive distributions in GSI's conformal framework, while simultaneously defining Markov decision process (MDP) states in GSE.
layer2.telemetry: Reconstruction error on holdout sets serves as a likelihood ratio test for model misspecification.

primitives.name: t-Distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding
primitives.verbatim_quote: t-SNE for joint model embeddings of map L games with original labels (left) and 13 k-means clusters (right).
primitives.assumptions: High-dimensional Gaussian neighborhood priors and low-dimensional Student-t distribution similarities with heavy tails.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Excessive early exaggeration hyperparameter (> 12) distorts global structure; perplexity < 5 loses robustness to noise.

layer2.mapping: t-SNE maps the autoencoder's latent space to a Euclidean visualization manifold where geodesic distances approximate Kullback-Leibler divergence between local conditional distributions.
layer2.telemetry: KL divergence between high and low dimensional distributions provides an out-of-sample test statistic for transferability across different game populations.

primitives.name: K-Means Clustering
primitives.verbatim_quote: By using raw action and state sequences instead of handcrafted features, our approach minimizes domain-specific biases, allowing patterns to emerge naturally from the data.
primitives.assumptions: Spherical cluster shapes, equal variance, and Voronoi tessellation of the embedding space.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Number of clusters \(k\) exceeding the true manifold dimension introduces spurious boundaries; too few clusters merge distinct attractors.

layer2.mapping: The cluster centroids define prototype policies in GSE's action-value function approximation, while pairwise cluster distances inform prior distributions in GSI's Bayesian updating.
layer2.telemetry: Calinski-Harabasz index tracks the separation-to-spread ratio, flagging optimal cluster counts for both interpretability and generalization.

primitives.name: Transformer Architecture
primitives.verbatim_quote: On the embedding side, future work should focus on autoencoder structures that induce specific latent structures like VAEs or VQ-VAEs, and the use of transformers to scale to bigger datasets and higher dimensions required to analyze the player bases of modern games.
primitives.assumptions: Self-attention mechanisms capture long-range dependencies, positional encodings preserve sequence order, and multi-head parallelism accelerates training.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Vanishing gradients in deep transformer stacks require residual connections; attention softmax saturates when key-query similarity exceeds embedding dimension square root.

layer2.mapping: Scaled dot-product attention computes conditional expectations over latent variables, directly implementing GSI's predictive state density estimation, while cross-attention modules enable hierarchical state-transition modeling in GSE.
layer2.telemetry: Attention sparsity patterns reveal emergent feature importance, serving as explainable AI metrics for both domains.

reasoning_traces.think: The foundational premise of this chapter lies in the transition from domain-dependent to domain-free play style identification. Traditional methods rely on handcrafted features derived from expert knowledge, which introduces bias and limits generalizability. The paper proposes an unsupervised CNN-LSTM autoencoder framework that learns latent representations directly from raw play trace data. This approach leverages the sequential nature of game actions while abstracting away the need for explicit feature engineering. The resulting latent space encodes meaningful distinctions among different play styles, enabling downstream tasks such as clustering and exploration. The mathematical underpinning involves encoding high-dimensional temporal sequences into compact latent vectors, followed by decoding to reconstruct the original data. The key innovation resides in the ability to perform style classification without domain abstraction, thereby removing expert dependency. The autoencoder's encoder function E maps input trajectories X to latent space Z, while the decoder D reconstructs X from Z. The training objective minimizes reconstruction loss, encouraging the model to retain essential style-related information in Z. This formulation allows for the application of standard clustering techniques on Z to identify distinct play styles. Furthermore, the latent space facilitates guided exploration of diverse play patterns, enhancing the realism and variety of AI agents. The theoretical alignment with game analytics suggests that this method supports adaptive gameplay systems where player styles inform dynamic adjustments in game mechanics. The empirical validation on MicroRTS demonstrates the efficacy of this approach in capturing nuanced behavioral differences. The implications extend beyond gaming to broader domains requiring unsupervised behavioral analysis.

reasoning_traces.think: Chapter window 3 focuses on evaluating clustering effectiveness across multiple AI-generated play traces using various embedding types. The core methodology involves computing standard clustering metrics—completeness, homogeneity, ARI, and AMI—to quantify how accurately learned representations reflect underlying agent behaviors. These metrics are averaged over maps A-K and analyzed individually for map L. The paper highlights that joint and actions-only encoders outperform states-only and handcrafted features, indicating that richer temporal and action-based information improves clustering fidelity. This supports a foundational assumption in GSI’s Bayesian inference engine where latent representations must encode sufficient discriminative features for accurate agent labeling. In GSE, such embeddings inform situational reasoning by enabling dynamic play-style recognition and transition prediction. The use of t-SNE visualizations further validates the robustness of these embeddings in capturing distinct agent behaviors. The findings suggest that incorporating multi-agent action sequences into latent spaces enhances both interpretability and predictive power for strategic modeling.
